assessment: The incumbent offers a predictable conversational sequence and printed access: seven frequent attendees explicitly value its repetition. That is a limiting observation against blaming the repeated structure itself. Five occasional attendees instead describe difficulty joining familiar conversations; uneven entry readiness is a hypothesis, not an established cause. Pair formation consumed eight and 13 minutes in two sessions, but partner changes do not establish proficiency mismatch. Positive reports were 49/72 for useful speaking and 48/72 for preparation; 72 slips cover 97 attendances, so these do not establish whole-attendance success rates. Coordination sometimes exceeded 90 minutes. Neither speaking allocation nor coordination components were measured.

openings.claim: A date-stamped, self-contained next-session preparation box on each printed sheet may reduce confusion between current and earlier tasks.
openings.delta: Retain the familiar session structure while making preparation independent of remembered sequence or prior attendance.
openings.prediction: Earlier-task answers decline when participants identify preparation from the revised sheet; persistent errors would weaken a version-confusion explanation.
openings.probe: At one session, anonymously compare next-task identification from current and revised printed layouts using counterbalanced order and different equivalent examples. Then track preparation identification and total coordination minutes over six sessions, including blank responses and total attendance.
assumptions: The intended next task can be fixed before printing.
Existing sheets can carry the box with little additional volunteer work.

openings.claim: A fresh shared opening prompt plus alternating timed speaking turns may help occasional attendees enter pairs while preserving the valued weekly routine.
openings.delta: Supply common conversational context and explicit turn access without requiring public proficiency labels or previous preparation.
openings.prediction: Pairs report fewer entry difficulties and show a higher minimum speaking time per partner; more timed speech without improved usefulness would limit the mechanism's value.
openings.probe: Within existing practice time, alternate matched ordinary and fresh-prompt timed rounds, reversing order across pairs. Observe turn distribution anonymously and collect separate usefulness and entry-difficulty slips; log setup time and weekly coordination.
assumptions: Volunteers can cue rounds within 75 minutes.
Combined changes test the package, not either component independently.
